steps.title: Meet I2C
steps.markdownContent:
### What is I2C?
**I2C** stands for **Inter-Integrated Circuit** (pronounced *"Eye-Squared-See"* or *"I-Two-C"*). Invented by Philips Semiconductor, it is a synchronous, multi-target, bidirectional serial communication bus.

The genius of I2C: it coordinates communication between up to **127 unique peripheral devices** over **just two shared wires**!

```
Arduino Uno (Controller)
       │           │
      SDA         SCL
       │           │
   ┌───┴───┐   ┌───┴───┐   ┌───┴───┐
   │  LCD  │   │ Clock │   │ Sensor│
   └───────┘   └───────┘   └───────┘
```

### The Two Roles on the Bus
1. **Controller (Master):** The Arduino Uno is the manager of the network. It initiates every communication session, drives the clock pulses, and commands target devices to send or receive data.
2. **Target (Peripheral / Slave):** The connected modules (such as LCD backpacks, sensors, or real-time clocks). They listen quietly on the bus and only respond when their unique address is called.

### Open-Drain & Pull-Up Resistors
How can dozens of devices share the exact same wires without short-circuiting each other? I2C uses an **open-drain** architecture:
- Both communication lines are passively held at +5V (**HIGH**) by **pull-up resistors** (typically 4.7kΩ).
- Connected devices only ever pull the line to Ground (0V / **LOW**) using internal transistors. They never force a 5V HIGH onto the wire.
- Because devices only pull LOW and never drive HIGH, two devices talking at once cannot create a direct short circuit between power and ground!

Test the interactive pull-up resistor simulator below to see why I2C lines cannot float and how proper pull-up values ensure crisp digital signals!

quickCheck.question: What is the primary role of the Arduino Uno when acting as the I2C Controller (Master)?
options: It manages the shared bus, generates clock pulses, and initiates all communication sessions with peripheral devices.
It cuts power to the circuit whenever more than two peripherals are connected.
It converts serial signals into high-frequency radio waves.
quickCheck.explanation: In an I2C network, the Controller initiates all transactions and provides the synchronizing clock pulse train for target peripheral devices.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Recall from Lesson 1 that the microcontroller acts as the central brain directing and coordinating peripherals in your robot.

quickCheck.question: Why are pull-up resistors required on the shared I2C communication lines?
options: They hold the open-drain lines at a stable HIGH voltage when idle so connected devices can pull the line LOW without creating a dead short circuit.
They amplify 5V signals up to 24V for long-distance industrial cables.
They slow down electrical current to keep wires from overheating.
quickCheck.explanation: I2C uses open-drain drivers. External pull-up resistors maintain lines at HIGH (5V) by default, allowing devices to safely pull lines to GND (LOW) to communicate.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: In Lesson 5, you learned that pull-up resistors keep inputs at a defined voltage rather than leaving lines floating in an undefined state.
